highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.159.0 introduces an experimental image-comparison package for testing rendered output.
highlights_body: The upcoming release also refines Ganesh texture-edge sampling and Tizen CPU blur selection. Linux x86 native assets are no longer included.

breaking.title: Move Linux x86 deployments to a supported architecture
breaking.body: Linux x86 native assets are no longer built or included in NuGet packages. Applications relying on those assets must move to a supported architecture before upgrading.

bullets.detail: SkiaSharp.Testing adds SKImageComparison for SKImage, SKBitmap and SKPixmap, with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets and error-magnitude gates. Comparisons default to exact unpremultiplied RGBA. The assembly is experimental; opt in by suppressing diagnostic SKIA4001 with NoWarn or a pragma.

Generate binary masks, channel differences, threshold maps, overlays and heatmaps to investigate image mismatches. Comparison results retain no native handles; returned difference images are independent SKImage instances that callers must dispose.
Filtered sampling clamps slightly inside texture subsets to avoid including undefined exterior texels. Ganesh texture-edge pixels may change; this does not change CPU or Graphite rendering.

bullets.lead: Tizen CPU blur selection applied correctly
bullets.detail: Tizen now applies its intended blur configuration to Skia itself, selecting the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent paths instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Blur output and performance may differ; Tizen rendering and performance were not measured locally for this change.

contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Restored the Uno Gallery and its view projects to the Windows sample solution.
